Ölüdeniz Paragliding Weather Guide

Understanding Babadağ Mountain's microclimate — and why Ölüdeniz has 280+ flyable days per year.

Why Is Ölüdeniz Weather So Good for Paragliding?

Babadağ Mountain creates a natural thermal factory. The mountain's south-facing slope absorbs solar radiation, heating the rock face. As warm air rises along the cliff, it creates reliable anabatic thermals that paragliders ride from 1,960m to over 2,500m. The Mediterranean Sea on three sides provides a stable air mass, and the Lycian mountain range blocks unpredictable weather from the north.

Key Wind Patterns

🌬️ Lodos (SW Wind)

Warm, gentle. Best for flying. Dominant April-October. Creates smooth lift along the coast. Perfect for tandem flights.

❄️ Poyraz (NE Wind)

Cold, gusty. Cancellation risk. More common November-March. Can create turbulence at launch. We ground all flights above 25 km/h Poyraz.

When Does Weather Cancel Flights?

  • 🚫 Wind speed above 25 km/h at launch altitude
  • 🚫 Cloud base below 1,500m (launch is at 1,960m)
  • 🚫 Active thunderstorm within 30km radius
  • 🚫 Rain or significant precipitation at launch

We check conditions at 06:00 on your flight day and notify you via WhatsApp. If cancelled, you get a full refund or free reschedule. See our safety policy.

Thermal Strength by Season

See best time to fly for the month-by-month breakdown.

  • April-May: Moderate thermals, smooth air, 20-35 min flights
  • June-August: Strong thermals, longest flights (35-50 min), summer flying details
  • September-October: Strong but stable, ideal for first-timers, 30-45 min
  • November: Variable, shorter flights, more cancellation risk

Morning vs. Afternoon Flights

Morning (08:00-11:00): Smoother air, gentler thermals. Best for nervous flyers. Afternoon (14:00-17:00): Stronger thermals, longer flights, more acrobatic potential. Sunset (~18:00-19:00): Calming air, golden light, limited spots.
